universal.question: What are the 3–5 most important things a user does, start to finish?
universal.whyItMatters: Each becomes a user story with acceptance criteria — the backbone of spec.md and the task list.

universal.question: What is explicitly NOT in the first release?
universal.whyItMatters: Writing down non-goals is the cheapest way to stop scope creep and keep the task list short.

universal.question: How will you know the first release worked — what number or observable outcome?
universal.whyItMatters: Turns 'done' into something testable and tells you what to measure after launch.

universal.question: Roughly how many users or visitors per month in the first year, and what's the busiest moment likely to be?
universal.whyItMatters: Drives scalability and cost: it decides whether free tiers are enough and what to load-test.

universal.question: What's the most you're willing to spend per month on hosting and services before you want to be alerted?
universal.whyItMatters: Becomes the budget alert threshold on every paid account — the main defense against surprise bills.

universal.question: What personal or sensitive data will you store or process (emails, payment info, health, location, children's data)?
universal.whyItMatters: Sets the security baseline and decides which privacy obligations apply.

universal.question: Which laws, policies, or standards apply — GDPR/UK GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, accessibility (WCAG), app-store policies, your company's policies?
universal.whyItMatters: Governance, risk & compliance requirements are far cheaper to design in than to retrofit.

universal.question: Where will your users be — EU/UK, California or other US states, elsewhere?
universal.whyItMatters: Decides which privacy laws apply (GDPR, CCPA and similar state laws) and whether international data transfers need covering in the privacy notice.

universal.question: List every piece of personal data you'll collect, and for each: why, and how long you'll keep it.
universal.whyItMatters: This becomes the PII inventory. Each field needs a purpose, a retention period, and a deletion path; anything without a purpose shouldn't be collected.

universal.question: Could children (under 16) use it?
universal.whyItMatters: Children's data brings parental-consent rules (GDPR, COPPA in the US). Most projects state a minimum age and don't target children.

universal.question: Will you use analytics, advertising, or tracking cookies or pixels, or sell or share personal data with anyone?
universal.whyItMatters: Tracking needs opt-in consent in the EU/UK; selling or sharing triggers CCPA's "Do Not Sell or Share" obligations.

universal.question: Which accessibility standard will you meet (WCAG 2.2 AA is recommended), and do any users rely on assistive technology you know of?
universal.whyItMatters: Accessibility is required in many places (ADA, the European Accessibility Act) and far cheaper to build in than to retrofit.

universal.question: What would 'wrong' look like — which errors would hurt users most, and how should they be caught?
universal.whyItMatters: Defines how you audit for correctness: which tests, validations, and alerts matter most.

universal.question: What speed is acceptable — page/screen load and action response times on a typical device and connection?
universal.whyItMatters: Gives performance a concrete target the plan and tests can check against.

universal.question: Which environments do you need (local, preview/staging, production), and who is allowed to deploy to production?
universal.whyItMatters: Shapes the deployment pipeline and the access-control part of the plan.

universal.question: Who owns each account (hosting, domain, third-party services), and where will credentials and secrets be stored?
universal.whyItMatters: Every component is an account someone must secure, pay for, and hand over if they leave.

universal.question: Who gets alerted when the site/app breaks or costs spike, and how (email, Slack, SMS)?
universal.whyItMatters: Monitoring without a recipient is just logging — this wires auditing and cost monitoring to a person.

universal.question: How will accessibility be tested — which automated tools, and which screen readers and devices for the manual pass?
universal.whyItMatters: Automated tools catch only about a third of issues; naming the manual checks puts them in the task list instead of leaving them to chance.

universal.question: Is there a deadline, and how many people (and AI agents) are building this?
universal.whyItMatters: Decides how finely tasks are split and which can run in parallel.

Static website.question: List every page and what each must contain.
Static website.whyItMatters: The sitemap is the spec for a static site — each page becomes one or more tasks.

Static website.question: Who writes and updates content, and how often?
Static website.whyItMatters: Decides whether editing Markdown/HTML is acceptable or a friendlier editing workflow is needed.

Static website.question: Does the site need a contact or signup form, and where should submissions go?
Static website.whyItMatters: A static site can't process forms itself — this adds a third-party service and a privacy disclosure.

Static website.question: Do you already own the domain, and who manages its DNS?
Static website.whyItMatters: DNS access is needed to go live and is a frequent last-minute blocker.

Static site with a blog.question: How are posts organized — categories, tags, series — and what does a post page show?
Static site with a blog.whyItMatters: Defines URL structure and the templates to build.

Static site with a blog.question: How many authors, and is there a draft → review → publish workflow?
Static site with a blog.whyItMatters: Decides whether git-based publishing is workable or authors need a CMS UI.

Static site with a blog.question: Do readers need RSS, an email newsletter, or both?
Static site with a blog.whyItMatters: Newsletters add a vendor and personal-data handling; RSS is free.

Static site with a blog.question: Are there existing posts to migrate, and do old URLs need redirects?
Static site with a blog.whyItMatters: Broken old links lose search ranking — redirects must be part of the plan.

Site with a backend/database.question: What are the main things the system stores (e.g. users, orders, posts) and how do they relate?
Site with a backend/database.whyItMatters: Becomes the data model — the hardest thing to change later.

Site with a backend/database.question: What roles exist, and what can each role see and do?
Site with a backend/database.whyItMatters: Authorization rules are a top source of security bugs; writing them down makes them testable.

Site with a backend/database.question: Which outside services must it integrate with (payments, email, maps, other APIs)?
Site with a backend/database.whyItMatters: Each integration is an account, a cost line, a failure mode, and often a data processor.

Site with a backend/database.question: How long must data be kept, and how are deletion and export requests handled?
Site with a backend/database.whyItMatters: Retention and deletion are core privacy-law obligations once you hold personal data.

Site with a backend/database.question: Does anything need to run in the background or on a schedule (emails, imports, reports)?
Site with a backend/database.whyItMatters: Background jobs need their own hosting, retries, and monitoring.

Site with a backend/database.question: How much data could you afford to lose (minutes? a day?), and how fast must you recover?
Site with a backend/database.whyItMatters: Sets backup frequency and the restore procedure you must test.

Phone app.question: List the main screens and how users move between them.
Phone app.whyItMatters: The screen map is the skeleton of the spec and the task list.

Phone app.question: What must work offline, and what happens when the connection returns?
Phone app.whyItMatters: Offline behavior changes data storage and sync design significantly.

Phone app.question: Which device features are needed (camera, location, contacts, biometrics)?
Phone app.whyItMatters: Each needs a permission prompt, a privacy-label entry, and a store-review justification.

Phone app.question: Which platforms and minimum OS versions must be supported?
Phone app.whyItMatters: Determines testing effort and which APIs are available.

Phone app.question: How will beta testing work (TestFlight, Play internal testing), and how are crashes reported?
Phone app.whyItMatters: Store review delays mean bugs must be caught before release.

Phone app.question: How will you force or encourage updates when an old app version breaks?
Phone app.whyItMatters: Old versions stay installed for months; the backend must handle them or block them.

Desktop app.question: Which operating systems and versions must be supported?
Desktop app.whyItMatters: Each OS adds build, signing, and test work.

Desktop app.question: Which files, folders, or other apps does it need to work with?
Desktop app.whyItMatters: File associations and OS integrations affect permissions, sandboxing, and installers.

Desktop app.question: Can users install software themselves, or will IT deploy it (admin rights, managed devices)?
Desktop app.whyItMatters: Corporate environments often block per-user installers and require MSI/PKG packages.

Desktop app.question: How will you get code-signing certificates, and who holds the signing keys?
Desktop app.whyItMatters: Unsigned apps trigger security warnings; leaked keys let attackers sign malware as you.

Desktop app.question: Will the app send crash reports or usage telemetry, and how do users consent?
Desktop app.whyItMatters: Telemetry is how you audit correctness in the field — and it's personal data.

static-website-build-approach/1.question: Which generator — Eleventy, Hugo, Jekyll, or another — and which theme, if any?
static-website-build-approach/1.whyItMatters: The wizard chose the category; the plan needs the specific tool.

static-website-build-approach/2.question: Astro or Next.js static export (or another framework)?
static-website-build-approach/2.whyItMatters: Astro ships less JavaScript by default; Next.js suits a later move to server rendering.

static-website-hosting/3.question: Who patches the server and renews TLS certificates, and how is the site deployed from git?
static-website-hosting/3.whyItMatters: Traditional hosting has no automatic deploys or patching unless you set them up.

static-website-analytics/2.question: Which consent tool will you use, and which visitor regions need a consent banner?
static-website-analytics/2.whyItMatters: Google Analytics uses cookies — EU/UK visitors need consent before tracking.

blog-build-approach/0.question: Which generator and theme?
blog-build-approach/0.whyItMatters: The wizard chose the category; the plan needs the specific tool.

blog-build-approach/1.question: What content types and fields does the CMS need (post, author, category, image fields)?
blog-build-approach/1.whyItMatters: This is the CMS content model — the equivalent of a database schema.

blog-build-approach/1.question: Which headless CMS, and how does publishing trigger a rebuild?
blog-build-approach/1.whyItMatters: The webhook between CMS and host is the most common silent failure.

blog-build-approach/2.question: Which plugins are must-haves, and who keeps them updated?
blog-build-approach/2.whyItMatters: Plugins are the main security risk on WordPress-style platforms.

blog-comments/2.question: What's the moderation policy — pre-approval, reporting, spam filtering?
blog-comments/2.whyItMatters: Custom comments make you responsible for abuse and spam handling.

backend-site-architecture/2.question: How will the API be versioned, and which origins are allowed by CORS?
backend-site-architecture/2.whyItMatters: Two deployables must stay compatible; CORS mistakes either break the app or open it up.

backend-site-architecture/3.question: What are the service boundaries, and which service owns which data?
backend-site-architecture/3.whyItMatters: Unclear ownership is the main way microservices turn into a distributed monolith.

backend-site-database/2.question: What are the main document shapes, and which queries must be fast?
backend-site-database/2.whyItMatters: Document databases are designed around access patterns, not normalization.

backend-site-database/3.question: Will the host give you a persistent disk, and how is the database file backed up?
backend-site-database/3.whyItMatters: SQLite needs a persistent disk — most serverless hosts don't have one.

backend-site-auth/0.question: What are the password rules, and are MFA, account lockout, and email verification required?
backend-site-auth/0.whyItMatters: Building auth yourself means specifying every one of these flows.

backend-site-auth/1.question: Which auth provider, and which login methods (email, social, passkeys)?
backend-site-auth/1.whyItMatters: Providers differ in free-tier limits and supported methods.

backend-site-auth/2.question: Which social providers (Google, GitHub, Microsoft, Apple)?
backend-site-auth/2.whyItMatters: Users without one of these accounts can't sign in.

backend-site-auth/3.question: When will logins be needed, and which pages and actions must stay public?
backend-site-auth/3.whyItMatters: Without auth, every write endpoint needs rate limiting and must hold no private data.

backend-site-hosting/0.question: Where does the database run relative to the function region, and will you use connection pooling?
backend-site-hosting/0.whyItMatters: Serverless functions far from the database, or without pooling, are slow and exhaust connections.

backend-site-hosting/3.question: Which specific cloud services (compute, database, secrets), and which infrastructure-as-code tool?
backend-site-hosting/3.whyItMatters: The big clouds offer many options — the plan must name them.

phone-app-architecture/1.question: React Native (with or without Expo) or Flutter?
phone-app-architecture/1.whyItMatters: The wizard chose the category; the plan needs the specific framework.

phone-app-backend/1.question: Which backend service, and who can read and write each table or collection (security rules)?
phone-app-backend/1.whyItMatters: With a backend-as-a-service, security rules are your only access control.

phone-app-backend/2.question: How long will old app versions be supported by the API?
phone-app-backend/2.whyItMatters: Mobile users don't update promptly — the API must stay backward compatible.

phone-app-auth/2.question: Which identity provider, and is mobile device management (MDM) required?
phone-app-auth/2.whyItMatters: Corporate SSO usually comes with distribution and device-policy requirements.

phone-app-push/1.question: Which events trigger a notification, and when do you ask for permission?
phone-app-push/1.whyItMatters: Asking too early gets denied; each notification type is a spec item.

phone-app-push/2.question: Which events trigger a notification, who can send marketing messages, and how do users opt out?
phone-app-push/2.whyItMatters: Marketing messages need consent and an opt-out.

desktop-app-architecture/1.question: Electron or Tauri?
desktop-app-architecture/1.whyItMatters: Tauri is much lighter and safer by default; Electron has the larger ecosystem.

desktop-app-storage/1.question: Must the local data be encrypted, and can users export or back it up?
desktop-app-storage/1.whyItMatters: Local data is only as safe as the user's disk and backups.

desktop-app-storage/2.question: What should happen when the same item is edited on two devices while offline?
desktop-app-storage/2.whyItMatters: The conflict rule is a product decision, not just a technical one.

desktop-app-distribution/1.question: Which stores, and does store sandboxing block any feature you need?
desktop-app-distribution/1.whyItMatters: Mac App Store sandboxing in particular restricts file and system access.

desktop-app-distribution/2.question: Where is the update feed hosted, and how will you stage rollouts and pull a bad release?
desktop-app-distribution/2.whyItMatters: The update channel can push code to every user — it needs a careful release process.

desktop-app-auth/2.question: Which identity provider, and what happens when a token expires while offline?
desktop-app-auth/2.whyItMatters: Desktop apps are often used offline; the expiry behavior must be decided.
